name: Extreme close-up
summary: A frame that holds only a part of a face, such as the eyes; the cut from a wide view to this frame sets a person against the world.
how: Frame the eyes as a band that fills the width of a 2.35:1 frame; use a lens of 75mm to 100mm.
Cut from a wide shot to the close-up with no medium shot between them.
Hold each close-up for 2 to 4 seconds and cut back to the wide view when the look ends.
In a painting, scale the head to 2 metres or more and keep the focus even over the full face.

origin.note: George Albert Smith inserts magnified close views into Grandma's Reading Glass.

adoptions.via: Carl Theodor Dreyer fills the frame with the face of Renée Falconetti in The Passion of Joan of Arc.
Sergio Leone cuts between the eyes of gunmen and a wide desert in A Fistful of Dollars, on a Techniscope 2.35:1 frame.
Chuck Close paints a huge frontal head from a photograph in Big Self-Portrait (1967–68).
Goblincore photographs fill the frame with a mushroom cap, a moss patch or a snail shell.

sources.title: Christopher Frayling, Sergio Leone: Something to Do with Death (Faber, 2000)
